content.thinking:
I'm planning the imports and structure for the file, pulling in builder, path, math, paint, and texture utilities, and confirming the build function should return the root Object3D.

Now I'm sketching the qilin's proportions and pose, then working out the body geometry using catmull sweeps with tapered radius functions for the barrel and neck, laying out coordinate paths for the rump, chest, and head to get the right silhouette.

For the head I'm shaping an elongated dragon-horse form with a capsule sweep from skull to muzzle, adding a snout chunk and planning to attach eye decals to the head surface, assuming the surface function can accept a sweep part directly.

Now I'm working out the eye decal placement using azimuthal positioning on the head and mirroring for symmetry, then moving on to leg construction -- front legs sweeping from shoulder to hoof with tapered radii, and back legs adding a hock bend through hip, stifle, and hock joints for that qilin-deer look.

Hooves get cloven shaping with two small offset boxes in dark gold, resting flush at floor level. I'm also thinking through coat texturing -- scale patterns on the back blending into a cream countershaded belly, deciding how to compose the paint function using surface normals to blend these regions.

Settling on a qilin color palette: deep teal scales with darker edges for the body, cream-gold belly, white-pink-cyan cloud mane, gold antlers and hooves, and vermilion flame tufts at the legs. Now moving to the tail design, planning an ox-like flowing sweep ending in a cloud tuft.

For the mane, I'm working through how to place cloud-puff spheres along the neck line since the path-following helper's signature is unclear, so I'll manually sample points along the path instead of relying on an unknown API.

Adding the gold curl ornaments at shoulders and haunches, then planning the cloud mane, chest beard, fetlock puffs, and tail tuft details, before sketching out the antler beam path with branching curves from the skull.

Now I'm adding tines branching off the antler beam at a few points along its length, with small glowing cyan spheres at the tips, then starting on the pointed ear shapes extruded at the sides of the head.

For the whiskers, I'm sweeping long flowing catmull curves from the muzzle with thin round caps in a gold-white tone, then moving on to sketch small subtle brow ridges instead of full horns.

Now I'm planning facial details: tiny dark nostril spheres, a dark mouth line, small white fang spikes, and a cloud-like gold beard under the chin, plus a frustum-shaped snout and jaw capsule for the dragon-like muzzle. I'm also sketching chimera touches -- a cream belly, cloud-textured chest, and flame-motif cards near the knees using a flame SVG texture.

Now I'm designing the mane using card frames oriented upward with a slight lean and flow direction, and sketching a wispy swirl-cloud SVG shape in white with cyan accents to use as the hair strand texture, considering a gradient fill for variety.

For body decoration, I'm planning a dorsal ridge of small gold spikes running along the spine from neck to tail, sampling points along the body path and placing each spike base slightly above the surface with an outward direction and length.

I'm also sketching gold belly plate stripes as horizontal bands under the chest, and considering a gold trim collar ring around the neck base, computing circle points around the neck path at a given parameter with an approximate ring radius rather than using a riskier surface loop approach.

Switching to using torus shapes aligned with the neck path's tangent direction instead, placing several gold rings along the neck at varying radii that taper down the neck, computing the radius and tangent at each point to orient the torus correctly.

Now I'm setting up the paint functions for the body, defining a teal scale pattern for most of the body and a cream/gold scale pattern for the belly, then combining them based on vertical position so the underside gets the lighter belly color while everything else gets the teal scales.

Mane puffs painted with cel white using icosahedron normal-based shading, with eyes sharing the head's skin surface. Working out the leg sweep paths for hooves now, defining tapered radius curves along smooth catmull-rom curves for front and back legs.

Adding thigh and shoulder bulges, then placing cloven hoof boxes at the foot base touching the floor.

Now I'm sketching a gold fetlock ring plus a fluffy white cloud puff and dewclaw detail around the lower leg, and adding small flame-card wisps behind the knees with outward-leaning frames for a subtle fire flow effect.

For the mane, I'm planning upward-facing cloud cards along a dorsal path running from neck to withers, leaning backward with a downward-back flow vector, distributing roughly twenty cards by sampling points along the offset neck curve and nudging them upward by a fraction of the radius.

For the tail, I'm shaping a catmull-rom curve sweeping back and up with a tapering radius, finishing in a tuft of cloud puffs and flame cards, keeping the tip tangent angled and comfortably above the floor.

Checking proportions, head top around 2.17 and antlers reaching 2.85 give a total height near 2.9, which feels right for a large creature.

I'm scaling the body down slightly — shoulder height around 1.15 with a thicker radius for a more horse-like silhouette, and trimming the antlers to 2.6 for better balance. Now I'm planning decorative details: gold swirl ornaments at the shoulders, hanging tassels, and a gold cloud-pattern decal applied onto the flank surface using a spiral SVG motif projected onto the body skin.

I'll skip the hanging tassel idea for simplicity, but I'm adding a glowing cyan chest jewel on a gold mount near the front of the body as a focal accent.

Now I'm working out the body's taper function to find where the chest is fullest, adjusting the radius formula so the front profile rounds out nicely instead of coming to a point.

Still working out jewel placement and spine positions...

Placing eyes using angular offsets around the head center, then building the jaw capsule, nose pad, nostrils, and mouth line with small ink rods for facial detail.

Adding fangs as small white spikes, gold brow ridge capsules above the eyes, and pale gold whiskers with puffed ends; considering beard cards under the chin but leaning toward soft cloud puffs instead. For the antler, I'm adding a second tier with glowing cyan sphere tips, and tallying up the flat color palette being used across the model.

Now I'm writing the sweep loop code for painting elements along paths, using a helper to offset Vector3 points and checking that all imports stay matched to what's actually used.

Setting up the mane cloud puffs with layered pastel cel colors, then switching to spiral swirls for the flank decoration using the spiral path generator.

Still defining flame frame orientations and gold sock paint logic for the legs...
